# How small businesses can use AI to make marketing work harder

![How small businesses can use AI to make marketing work harder](https://a.storyblok.com/f/102007/1280x720/a60280bccb/ss3-man-computer-smiling.jpg/m/filters:quality\(90\))

Connect

* * *

Posted: **Thu 5th Nov 2026**

**Marketing can sometimes feel like a job in itself when running a small business. There are customers to reach, content to create, emails to send, social media to manage and results to keep track of.** 

For a small team or a business owner, finding the time and budget to manage all this can be difficult. 

AI can help. Used thoughtfully, it can take repetitive work off your plate, help you understand your audience and give you more time to focus on the parts of marketing that require your experience and creativity. 

The key is to use AI to make better-informed marketing decisions and create content that is genuinely useful to your customers. 

## AI and marketing: What business owners need to know 

AI tools can analyse information, identify patterns, generate ideas and help with repetitive tasks. For a small business, that could mean using AI to brainstorm a campaign, understand customer feedback, draft an email or analyse content performance. 

One of its biggest benefits is saving time. 

Rather than starting every piece of content from a blank page, you can use AI to create an initial structure or generate ideas. You can then bring your own knowledge and experience to the final result. 

That human input is important, particularly in local communities. AI doesn’t know your customers in the same way you do, and it cannot replace the relationships you have built with them. 

Think of AI as an assistant, not your marketing department. 

## **Practical ways AI can support your marketing** 

There are plenty of ways AI can become part of your marketing without taking over. 

### **1\. Market research and audience analysis** 

AI can help you organise information about your customers, identify common questions and spot themes in feedback. 

For example, if customers regularly ask about the same part of your service, that could highlight an opportunity for a blog post, social media series, [email](https://www.growlondonlocal.london/learn-something/how-email-marketing-helps-you-connect-with-customers/) or website update. 

You can also use AI to help identify customer groups and think about what each one might need from your business. 

### 2\. Find content and campaign ideas 

If you’re struggling to think of something to post or promote, AI can help with brainstorming. 

Give it information about your business, your audience and your goals and ask it to suggest content themes, campaign ideas or ways to promote specific products or services. 

### **3\. Create marketing content** 

AI can draft blogs, website copy, social media posts, newsletters and advertising copy. 

It can also help turn one piece of content into several formats. For example, a blog post could become a series of social posts or a newsletter. 

### 4\. Personalise customer communications 

AI can help you create different versions of a message for different audiences. 

For example, a new customer might need an introduction to your business, while an existing customer might be more interested in new products or special offers. 

Personalisation is not about creating hundreds of individual messages. Even small changes in language and content can make communications feel more relevant. 

If you’re using customer information for marketing, [GOV.UK's guidance on direct marketing](https://www.gov.uk/marketing-advertising-law/direct-marketing) explains requirements around permission, contacting customers and giving people the ability to opt out. 

### **5\. Support social media** 

AI can help you plan a social media calendar, brainstorm post ideas, write captions and suggest different ways to present the same message. 

It can also help you analyse which posts are getting the most engagement. 

But [social media](https://www.growlondonlocal.london/learn-something/social-media-marketing-small-businesses-london/) still needs to feel social. Your customers want to see the people and personality behind the business, so do not let AI make every post sound polished but impersonal. 

### **6\. Analyse marketing performance** 

Marketing produces a lot of data, but knowing how to analyse it can be challenging. 

AI can help you identify patterns in website traffic, email engagement, social media performance or campaign results. 

Instead of asking whether a campaign “worked”, look at what the results can teach you. Which audience responded? Which message attracted attention? What could you change next time? 

### **7\. Automate repetitive tasks** 

AI can help reduce some of the routine or administrative work involved in marketing. 

You might use automation to schedule content, organise customer enquiries, summarise information or help manage repetitive workflows. 

## Getting started with AI for marketing 

You don’t need to change your entire marketing strategy overnight. 

1.  **Start with a clear goal:** Decide what you are trying to achieve. Do you want more website visitors, enquiries, sales, repeat customers or greater awareness? 
    
2.  **Identify where you need help:** Look at the parts of marketing that take the most time. Is it content creation, campaign planning, social media or analysing results? Start there. 
    
3.  **Choose tools that fit your business:** You don’t need to buy every AI tool available. [Grow London Local's digital support](https://www.growlondonlocal.london/digital-support/) offers free resources for small businesses, including digital tools and AI, and access to Business Support Managers who can help you find relevant support. 
    
4.  **Give AI useful information:** The more context you provide, the more useful the result is likely to be. Explain your audience, tone of voice, objectives and what makes your business different. 
    
5.  **Keep a human quality check:** Decide what needs checking before anything

One of the best outcomes of the AI boom is that it’s helping small and local businesses get results that used to be out of reach. Now, a business owner or one-person marketing team can pull customer insights from across the web, create a high-converting email sequence customized to each lead, and spin up a unique cost calculator that helps qualify prospects fast.

The new challenge is figuring out where to use this incredibly powerful and versatile tool.

In this guide, we’ve detailed 35 ways to use AI in marketing for social media, paid advertising, and more. These aren’t generic ideas like “use it to write captions.” Each idea shows how to use AI for a specific marketing task so you can get results right now.

## 35 ways to use AI in marketing for:

*   [Social media](https://localiq.com/blog/ai-in-marketing/#how-to-use-ai-for-social-media)
*   [Local SEO](https://localiq.com/blog/ai-in-marketing/#how-to-use-ai-for-local-seo)
*   [Your website](https://localiq.com/blog/ai-in-marketing/#how-to-use-ai-for-a-better-website)
*   [Reviews and reputation](https://localiq.com/blog/ai-in-marketing/#how-to-use-ai-for-reviews-and-reputation)
*   [Email and SMS](https://localiq.com/blog/ai-in-marketing/#how-to-use-ai-for-email-and-sms)
*   [Paid ads](https://localiq.com/blog/ai-in-marketing/#how-to-use-ai-for-paid-ads)
*   [Customer communications](https://localiq.com/blog/ai-in-marketing/#how-to-use-ai-for-customer-communications)
*   [Tips for using AI in marketing](https://localiq.com/blog/ai-in-marketing/#tips-for-using-ai-in-marketing)

## How to use AI for social media

[Social media](https://localiq.com/products/social-ads/) works best when you post what your audience actually responds to. These ideas help you [learn from competitors](https://localiq.com/blog/competitive-insights/), your own past content, and online conversations so each post has a better shot at engaging your ideal audience.

### Analyze competitors’ top-performing posts

Pick three to five competitors, including a couple outside your area that are great at social. Screenshot their 10 [most-engaged posts](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2022/03/10/facebook-post-ideas) from the last few months and upload them to AI. Ask: “Categorize these by topic, format, and opening hook. What patterns show up in the posts with the most comments? Suggest 10 ideas for my business that use those patterns but cover topics they’re missing.”

![Social media tips - Dentist posts on TikTok.](//localiq.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)

_Find businesses in your niche and feed their best-performing posts to AI._

Begin testing a few each week. Keep track of which work for your [unique audience](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/ws/2022/05/11/target-audience).

👋 **Want more?** Here’s [14 No-Brainer Ways to Use AI for Social Media (+20 Prompts)](https://localiq.com/resources/ai-for-social-media/?cid=Web_LiQ_Any_InContent_Guide_AIforSocial_Download%20&itm_source=localiq&itm_medium=blog&itm_campaign=incontent_links)

### Find themes in your most successful content

Export six to 12 months of post data from Meta Business Suite or your platform’s analytics. Upload the file to AI and ask: “Compare my top 10 posts to my bottom 10 by engagement rate. What’s different about topic, format, length, posting time, and whether people appear in the photo?”

Turn the answers into three simple rules, like “Show the team” or “Lead with a question.” Use those conclusions to guide [future social posts](https://localiq.com/blog/what-to-post-on-instagram/), whether you write them or have help from AI.

### Quickly repurpose larger assets into social posts

Pick one bigger piece of content, like a [blog post](https://localiq.com/blog/content-marketing-for-small-businesses/), video, workshop recording, or newsletter. Upload it to AI with three of your best past posts as voice examples. Ask: “Turn this into a carousel outline, two short video scripts under 30 seconds, a Facebook post, and a Google Business Profile post. Use a different takeaway for each.”

Edit, then spread the new posts across the next two weeks so one asset covers two weeks of posts.

### Turn customer projects into engaging posts

Pick a project (or product) with a clear before and after, then gather photos, short video clips, and the customer’s review. Upload them to AI and ask: “Write a five-slide carousel that tells this story: the problem, what we did, the result, and a call to action. Then write a 20-second video script with on-screen text.”

![Instagram ad examples - Ad from Sunday](//localiq.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)

_Use AI to turn basic before-and-after images and posts into [engaging social content](https://localiq.com/blog/social-media-traffic/) like videos and carousels._

Get the customer’s okay before sharing, and ask if you can tag them. Their social media network may be your next customers.

# The marketer’s guide to Conversational AI: What it is and how it works

Published on April 03, 2026/Last edited on April 03, 2026/10 min read

![A glowing search bar with a blinking cursor, surrounded by various application and data icons, on a purple to orange gradient background.](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/b7pblshe/marketing-prod/c18908ede4d6d7973a4adb2ff09e2eae18d7f346-3840x2160.png?auto=format&fit=max&w=3840&q=75)

AUTHOR

![A smiling woman with long blonde hair wearing a teal blouse stands against a gray background.](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/b7pblshe/marketing-prod/917432328de7216909471c04f0a4f65a65e21c36-512x512.jpg?auto=format&fit=max&w=3840&q=75)

###### Lexie Haggerty

Senior Product Marketing Manager, Braze

They say you can tell a lot about a person by how loudly they scream “Speak to a representative!” into their phone after a dead-end interaction with a chatbot. We’ve all been there: Trapped in a fruitless loop powered by rigid, rules-based logic that simply doesn’t understand what we need.

But those frustrating experiences are rapidly moving into the rearview mirror, thanks to a new era of AI. Basic two-way interactions once limited by pre-defined scripts are being replaced by robust, human-like conversations. They’re powered by a new term you might have heard floating around: Conversational AI (CAI), which provides specific, contextual responses rooted in a deep, real-time understanding of the customer.

If you’re a marketer looking to integrate this technology into your customer engagement strategy, read on to learn the fundamentals of CAI, how it works, and how it can help you set your brand apart.

### **What is Conversational AI?**

At its core, Conversational AI (CAI) enables computers to understand and respond to human language in a natural, fluid manner. It isn’t just about chatting; it’s about facilitating human-like dialogue. CAI works by combining foundational large language models (LLMs), brand-specific context, and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to facilitate human-like dialogue through the use of [AI agents](https://www.braze.com/resources/articles/ai-agents-marketing).

![Smiling presenter holding a microphone in front of a purple background with Braze branding and the text “Minutes to Market – Solve SMS chaos.”](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/b7pblshe/marketing-prod/4aa6a0acd9e5be467b26b267a98424f555bd73c1-3840x2160.png?auto=format&fit=max&w=3840&q=75)

Let’s break it down further:

#### _How it works_

Before a response reaches a customer’s screen, a sophisticated process occurs under the hood. For marketers, understanding these components is key to building a strong CAI strategy. You don’t need to be an AI expert—you just need to know enough to be dangerous! Let’s take a look at all the components that power a conversational AI interaction.

![A table explaining four key components of a Conversational AI system: Foundational LLMs, Additional Data and Context, Channels, and Guardrails, detailing their roles and providing examples for each.](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/b7pblshe/marketing-prod/e5ffa6105292befab88a7847b67063bbcd48b41d-2400x1712.png?auto=format&fit=max&w=3840&q=75)

### **Bringing it all together**

A foundational LLM is a powerful engine, but it isn't ready for your customers out of the box. It needs to be given relevant and accurate context to respond in a way that sounds and feels like your brand.

Let’s look at how these components work together. Pretend you’re a marketer for an eCommerce skincare brand building a virtual beauty assistant:

1.  **The agent & LLM:** You prompt your AI agent (powered by a foundational LLM) to act as a "skincare expert" with the goal of helping customers find the right products for their needs.
2.  **The context:** You give the agent context by connecting it to your product catalog, customer data, and FAQs, including detailed descriptions of each product and the specific skincare concerns they treat.
3.  **The interaction:** A customer reaches out on a channel like WhatsApp asking, "What should I buy for my dry skin?"
4.  **The reasoning:** Instead of just providing a link to a generic quiz, the agent uses its reasoning to engage in a dialogue. It might analyze the customer's past purchase history to avoid duplicates and recommend a custom routine based on the specific product knowledge you’ve given it.
5.  **The guardrails:** Throughout the chat, guardrails ensure the agent stays on brand, only recommends products you actually sell, and maintains a helpful, professional tone.

By combining the "brain" of the LLM with your brand's specific knowledge, the agent delivers a concierge-style experience that feels human, but scales effortlessly.

### **Conversational AI vs. traditional chatbots**

To help soldify your knowledge of this cutting-edge technology, let’s take a look at how it compares to the chatbots of the past. The difference isn't just technical; it’s a total shift in the customer experience.

![Table comparing features of traditional chatbots and conversational AI agents.](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/b7pblshe/marketing-prod/b421cb94b24e4f10a2164071a127cc7e89617569-2400x1962.png?auto=format&fit=max&w=3840&q=75)

### **Why marketers need CAI now**

In 2026, one-sided marketing campaigns—what we call "digital shouting"—simply don't work. As brands continue to produce more content to gain market share, billions of marketing messages are ignored or deleted. Brands today are getting lost in the crowd and need new, compelling ways to stand out; in fact, 52% of consumers say that most brands they see online have no memorable distinction, according to the [2026 Global Customer Engagement Review](https://www.braze.com/resources/reports-and-guides/global-customer-engagement-review).

Consumers want connection. [78% of customers are already messaging with brands on messaging apps like WhatsApp](https://www.forbes.com/councils/forbestechcouncil/2023/09/19/the-rise-of-messaging-in-consumer-engagement-what-brands-should-know/)—and they love it because today's consumers value quick, direct communication. The benefits of CAI for the modern marketer include:

*   **Meeting customers where they are:** Instead of forcing customers to a website, you can conduct a full, rich interaction inside the messaging apps they already use, like WhatsApp or SMS/RCS.
*   **Building two-way value exchanges:** Conversations allow you to give and receive. Instead of a one-way "Buy this!” or “Take this action!" push, you can ask clarifying questions to provide a better recommendation, turning a promotion into a helpful service.
*   **Driving frictionless commerce:** By addressing product concerns in real time, you save the customer the work of doing their own research. Serv
